outcome: No case of any of the 14 conjectures Wikipedia's article numbers under this heading (Direct Summand, Canonical Element, Improved New Intersection, Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor, Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities, etc.) was settled in the window. The one concrete piece of post-window movement found is in a closely related, commonly co-discussed homological conjecture not itself among the 14: VandeBogert and Walker proved a stronger form of the Total Rank Conjecture (a coarser corollary of the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture) for rings of characteristic two, revised April 2024 and published in Duke Math. J. in February 2025. No AI involvement in that or any other lead.
summary: Wikipedia's article 'Homological conjectures in commutative algebra' enumerates 14 specific numbered conjectures from Melvin Hochster's program (Zero Divisor Theorem, Bass's Question, Intersection Theorem, New Intersection Theorem, Improved New Intersection Conjecture, Direct Summand Conjecture, Canonical Element Conjecture, Existence of Balanced Big Cohen-Macaulay Modules, Cohen-Macaulayness of Direct Summands, Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor, Strong Direct Summand Conjecture, Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen-Macaulay Algebras, Serre's Conjecture on Multiplicities, Small Cohen-Macaulay Modules Conjecture). I searched for post-26-January-2024 movement on each by name and found none: no new proofs, no new cases settled, and no retractions. The Direct Summand Conjecture and Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen-Macaulay Algebras Conjecture were resolved by Andre/Bhatt/Heitmann-Ma well before the frozen date (2016-2018) and remain the state of the art; nothing moved after. Serre's positivity conjecture is still open with its most recent partial case (Skalit) from 2019. The one substantive post-window item I found in the broader neighborhood of 'homological conjectures in commutative algebra' as a named research subject is Keller VandeBogert and Mark E. Walker's paper on the Total Rank Conjecture in characteristic 2 (arXiv:2305.09771), whose v1 (May 2023) predates the window but whose v2 (11 April 2024) and Duke Mathematical Journal publication (February 2025, vol. 174 issue 2) postdate it; it proves a stronger form of the Total Rank Conjecture — a coarser corollary of the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture — for characteristic-two rings, and separately proves an extension over non-Cohen-Macaulay rings containing any field. The Total Rank/Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture is not one of the 14 conjectures this Wikipedia article numbers, though it is frequently discussed in the same literature and courses under the 'homological conjectures' banner (e.g. Hochster's own surveys). I also found a 2026 preprint (arXiv:2607.26118) exhibiting explicit counterexamples to a *local variant* of Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks formulated by Lima-Pereira, Nuno-Ballesteros, Orefice-Okamoto and Tomazella for complete-intersection singularities — but this is a variant conjecture these authors themselves introduced, not a case of anything on Wikipedia's list, so it is out of scope under Section 3.1 and I did not use it as the basis for status. I separately investigated an AI system called Rethlas (arXiv:2605.25259, May 2026) reported to have resolved several open problems in commutative ring theory and Boij-Soderberg theory fully autonomously with human verification; its GitHub results page lists the specific problems solved (from Cahen-Fontana-Frisch-Glaz's 'Open Problems in Commutative Ring Theory' and Erman-Sam's Boij-Soderberg survey), and none of them are any of the 14 homological conjectures on this page or the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks family — they are unrelated open questions that happen to share the broad subfield label 'commutative algebra'. I also checked a 2025 line of work on stable equivalences of Morita type and the Auslander-Reiten conjecture; this belongs to the representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras (a distinct, though loosely analogous, family of 'homological conjectures' in a different subfield) and is not part of the Hochster program this Wikipedia article documents, so I did not use it either. Net: no true movement on any of the 14 listed conjectures; the closest thing to a hit is a genuinely human-authored partial result on a related-but-distinct conjecture, so I classify this record as 'progress' with low confidence that it belongs strictly in scope, flagged via competing_reading.
competing_reading: A stricter reading of Section 3.1 would hold that since the Total Rank Conjecture is not one of the 14 conjectures Wikipedia numbers under this exact heading, and is a genuinely different statement (about total Betti numbers/ranks) rather than a restriction of any of the 14, the correct status is 'open' with no_change_found true, treating VandeBogert-Walker as a 'related problem' in the Section 3.1 sense rather than a 'case of the problem'. Under that reading this record would be 'open'/no_change_found instead of 'progress'. I chose 'progress' because the bullet's statement is the broad umbrella phrase 'Homological conjectures in commutative algebra' (not a single conjecture), the Wikipedia article's own lead frames the numbered list as illustrative of a research program rather than an exhaustive closed set, and Hochster's own surveys of 'the homological conjectures' regularly include Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks-type rank statements alongside the 14. Reasonable people could pick either classification.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the dataset intends 'homological conjectures in commutative algebra' to mean exactly the 14 conjectures enumerated in the linked Wikipedia article, or the broader named research program as the field itself uses the term (which would include Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks/Total Rank Conjecture, Auslander-Reiten-type statements, etc.).
